title: A number is not yet a physical quantity
question: Why can a numerically correct expression still be physically meaningless?
answerPreview: A physical result must preserve its quantity meaning, not only its dimension, when we change the units used to express it.
summary: Distinguish quantities, quantity values, numerical values, kinds, dimensions, and meaningful dimensionless ratios; then test bounded expressions and unit conventions without treating consistency as empirical evidence.

observationStage.title: International System of Units (SI) defining anchors
observationStage.question: Which values are exact definitions, and where does practical uncertainty enter?

items.label: Caesium-133 transition frequency
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly to define the second. A practical clock realizes the definition through a physical procedure and reports the uncertainty of that realization or measurement.

items.label: Speed of light in vacuum
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly, linking realization of the metre to the second. A practical length realization or light-path measurement still has method-dependent uncertainty.

items.label: Planck constant
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly as an action scale used in defining the kilogram. A practical realization transfers that definition through an experiment whose result carries realization uncertainty.

observationStage.conclusion: The displayed numbers are fixed defining values, not three uncertainty-free measurements. Definitions establish exact references; practical realizations and measurements connect physical apparatus to those references and carry stated uncertainty.

caveats: Exact defining values do not make practical realizations or measurements uncertainty-free.

guidedBlocks.title: A number is only one part of a quantity value
body: The number 30 does not say whether we mean 30 seconds, 30 metres, or 30 kilograms.

A quantity is a property with a magnitude. A quantity value expresses that magnitude as a number and a reference, usually a unit: 30 m is a length value, and its numerical value is 30 when the chosen unit is the metre.
Changing the unit can change the numerical value without changing the quantity. The same length value can be written 2 m or 200 cm.
caveats: This activity treats scalar quantities; vector and tensor components require additional structure.

guidedBlocks.title: International System of Units definitions fix anchors; laboratories realize them
body: The International System of Units (SI) second is defined by fixing the caesium-133 ground-state hyperfine transition frequency Delta_nu_Cs at exactly 9 192 631 770 Hz, where Hz is s^-1.

The metre is defined through the fixed speed of light c = 299 792 458 m s^-1. This definition links length to the second; practical realization uses specified experimental procedures rather than treating every light-path measurement as exact.
The Planck constant h is fixed at exactly 6.626 070 15 x 10^-34 J s. Its quantity kind is action, and together with the second and metre definitions it participates in the SI definition of mass.
A unit definition fixes the reference. A practical realization is a documented method for producing or measuring against that reference, with an uncertainty appropriate to the realization.
caveats: Exact defining constants do not make practical realizations uncertainty-free.

guidedBlocks.title: Dimensions and quantity kinds answer different questions
body: Metres and centimetres are different unit coordinates for the same kind of quantity, length, so their values can be converted and compared.
Matching dimensions are necessary but not sufficient for matching quantity kinds. Energy and torque have the same dimension, but they are not the same kind of quantity.
A length cannot be added to a time. No multiplicative conversion factor makes that sum describe one quantity kind.
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: VIM3 entries 1.2 and 1.7; NIST SP 811 chapters 7-8
caveats: NIST SP 811 predates the SI changes effective 20 May 2019 and is not used here for current SI definitions.

guidedBlocks.title: A dimensionless ratio can still carry meaning
body: Dividing one length by another length cancels the length dimension. For example, a 2 m height divided by a 4 m reference height gives the dimensionless ratio 0.5.
Dimensionless does not mean meaningless. A ratio can encode shape, efficiency, probability, refractive index, an angle convention, or another physically important comparison.
Always name what was compared and any convention used; the zero dimension vector alone does not tell us the quantity kind or interpretation.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; JCGM 200:2012
caveats: Some dimensionless quantity values depend on conventions, including angle units and normalization choices.

guidedBlocks.title: A necessary check, not a proof
body: A dimensionally inconsistent equation cannot represent the proposed quantity relationship.
A dimensionally consistent equation can still combine different quantity kinds or use a wrong model, wrong parameter, or unsupported assumption.
The workshop computes a contract check. It does not make an empirical observation.
caveats: A dimension match does not identify a quantity kind.

technicalBlocks.title: Dimensions form exponent vectors
body: Represent a dimension by exponents over base quantities. The Tour uses seven conventional International System of Quantities (ISQ) base-quantity dimensions in this order: time, length, mass, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.
Average speed has vector (-1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0); energy has (-2, 2, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0). Quantities multiply or divide, while their dimension-exponent vectors add or subtract.
The general dimension representation permits rational exponents. This activity's bounded named expressions use integer exponents only.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; JCGM 200:2012
caveats: The base-quantity dimensions are a conventional basis, not seven intrinsic dimensions of nature.

technicalBlocks.title: Multiplicative coherent unit changes transform numerical values
body: If q = {q}[Q], then choosing a new unit [Q]' = a[Q] changes the numerical value to {q}' = {q}/a while q itself is unchanged.
The dimensional builder applies declared multiplicative scale transforms only after binding the sample magnitude to the selected target quantity kind.
The builder excludes affine temperature conversions and electromagnetic centimetre-gram-second (CGS) conventions; its mechanical CGS option is limited to centimetre, gram, and second scaling.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; NIST SP 811e2008
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: BIPM section 2.3; NIST SP 811 chapter 8 and Appendix B
caveats: Only multiplicative coherent conversions declared by this activity are in scope.

technicalBlocks.title: Natural units change coordinates, not dimensional meaning
body: A natural-unit convention chooses dimensional constants such as c, hbar, or k_B as reference scales and assigns them numerical value 1 in that coordinate system.

Writing c = 1 can make time and length share one numerical coordinate, but it does not erase their dimensional relationship. To return to SI coordinates, restore the powers of c, hbar, and k_B required by the target dimension.

For example, the coordinate x^0 = c t has length dimension. Natural-unit notation may write x^0 = t after setting c = 1; restoring SI coordinates requires x^0 = c t, not a claim that seconds and metres are identical units.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; NIST SP 811e2008
caveats: Restoration factors depend on the declared natural-unit convention and target quantity dimension.

technicalBlocks.title: Five-axis Atlas declarations and seven-axis Tour checks are separate audits
body: The historical Atlas source-audit model uses five axes and its own treatment of amount of substance. The Tour uses the seven-axis International System of Quantities (ISQ) model: time, length, mass, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.

The current typed Atlas engine reports exactly 68 known source declaration dimension conflicts in that historical five-axis audit. They are source-audit findings, not sixty-eight equations repaired by the Tour.

This lesson's seven-axis contract neither normalizes nor repairs those declarations. The 68 conflicts remain tied to their source basis and implementation revision, and this activity does not recompute or resolve them.
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: PHYSICS_TOUR_MASTER_PLAN.md Chapter 1 technical extension and Definition of done; Atlas formula dimension declarations and source-audit ledger
caveats: This lesson does not supply independent evidence for the historical source declarations.

equationSteps.label: International System of Units fixed defining anchors
equationSteps.explanation: The SI fixes these numerical values to define the second, link the metre to the second, and link the kilogram to h. Laboratories still use documented realization procedures whose practical results carry realization uncertainty.
caveats: Exact defining values do not make practical realizations or measurements uncertainty-free.

equationSteps.label: Dimensionless ratio
equationSteps.expression: r = H / H_ref; dim(r) = L / L = 1
equationSteps.explanation: The dimensions cancel, but r still means the stated comparison between a height and its reference height. Its interpretation is not supplied by the zero dimension vector alone.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; JCGM 200:2012
caveats: Dimensionless does not imply quantity-kind-free or convention-free.

equationSteps.label: Natural-unit coordinate convention
equationSteps.expression: x^0 = c t; with c = 1, x^0 = t; restoring SI: x^0 = c t
equationSteps.explanation: Setting c to numerical unity is a coordinate convention. Restoring SI coordinates inserts c so the time coordinate is expressed with length dimension.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; NIST SP 811e2008
caveats: The required restoration factors depend on the target dimension and all constants set to numerical unity.

equationSteps.label: Spoken relationship
equationSteps.expression: average speed is path length divided by elapsed time
equationSteps.explanation: The words identify the quantity kinds and the averaging interval before numerical values enter.
caveats: Average speed uses total path length, not displacement, and does not assert constant instantaneous speed.

equationSteps.label: Symbolic relationship
equationSteps.explanation: Division of quantities corresponds to subtraction of the elapsed-time exponent from the path-length exponent.
caveats: This is the definition of average speed over the selected interval.

equationSteps.label: Dimension relationship
equationSteps.explanation: Any multiplicative coherent unit representation of average speed transforms as length per time.
caveats: The dimension alone does not distinguish average speed from velocity or other length-per-time quantity kinds.

checkpoints.prompt: Before switching units: a rod has quantity value 2 m. What numerical value expresses the same length in centimetres?
checkpoints.explanation: A centimetre is one hundredth of a metre, so the numerical value is 100 times larger while the quantity value represents the same length.

caveats: This source-authored answer is not a record of a learner prediction or runtime evaluation.

checkpoints.prompt: A proposed equation has the same dimensions on both sides. What has the audit established?

choices.label: It passed one necessary consistency check
Both sides must be the same quantity kind

checkpoints.explanation: Matching dimensions are necessary, but quantity kind, model assumptions, and empirical evidence require separate checks.
